fields.ic_name: ARM Serial Wire Debug (SWD) — ADIv5 (ARM IHI 0031C)
fields.constraints_present: partial — ADIv5 specifies protocol-level behavior + 2-pin SW-DP / 4-pin JTAG-DP / mode-switchable SWJ-DP architecture but does not specify PDK / floorplan / SDC constraints. Per-device + per-board integration constraints are non-protocol but commonly required.
typical_per_device_constraints: SWD pins (SWCLK + SWDIO + optional nTRST + optional SWO) shall be dedicated debug pins, not shared with functional logic (except SWJ-DP shares with JTAG via the same physical pads).
Per-target SWCLK max frequency: implementation-defined; Cortex-M0+ typical 10-24 MHz; Cortex-A SoCs with full DAP up to 50-100 MHz.
Per-target tSU(SWDIO) / tH(SWDIO) / tPD(SWDIO) timing parameters specified in the device datasheet.
SWDIO output drive strength must be sufficient to overcome the host probe's pull-up + interconnect capacitance.
ESD protection on SWD pins per pin-class HBM / CDM / MM requirements (e.g. ±2 kV HBM minimum for production Arm MCUs).
Slew-rate control on SWDIO and SWCLK drivers reduces reflections on long probe cables.
Internal pull-up on SWDIO recommended (so SWDIO defaults to HIGH = line-reset-friendly when no probe connected).
Internal pull-down on SWCLK optional (some SoCs implement this, others rely on the probe).
Optional SWO trace pin requires a separate TPIU output buffer + level shifter.
typical_per_board_constraints: SWCLK routed as a controlled-impedance trace; keep length short for high-speed (>20 MHz) operation.
SWDIO bidirectional driver — board-level series resistor (typically 0 Ω - 22 Ω) on SWDIO for level matching and ESD protection.
Pull-up resistor on SWDIO (typically 4.7 kΩ - 10 kΩ to VDD-IO) keeps line HIGH when probe disconnected.
Pull-down resistor on SWCLK (optional, typically 10 kΩ to GND) keeps line at known quiescent level.
Pull-up on nTRST (if implemented) so the SWJ-DP can run when the tester is present.
Termination on SWCLK if rise/fall times approach board-trace propagation delay (rarely needed below 50 MHz).
Connector pin allocation: ARM 10-pin Cortex Debug header (SWCLK=pin4, SWDIO=pin2, GND=pin5/3, VTREF=pin1, RESET=pin10, KEY=pin7); or ARM 20-pin Cortex+ETM header; or TC2050 Tag-Connect footprint.
VTREF (target voltage sense) routed to the probe so the probe knows target VDD-IO (auto level-matching probes).
Optional SRST line — a separate target-reset signal allowing the host probe to assert hardware reset (some probes connect to the SoC's NRST pin).
Multi-drop SWD board: shared SWDIO/SWCLK trace must be controlled-impedance with low total bus capacitance (typically < 25 pF total).
SWO trace pin routing: dedicated trace to the probe's UART RX (or trace capture), typically short and impedance-matched.
fields.process_technology_independence: ADIv5 is process-independent. Any logic-process technology that can implement flip-flops + a small shift-register + an internal AHB/APB bus master can implement the SW-DP + MEM-AP. Most modern Arm-based MCUs (28 nm - 180 nm) include ADIv5 as a hard IP block licensed from Arm.
fields.notes: ARM IHI 0031C (1996-2022 multi-revision) does not list SDC / UPF / DFT constraints because the standard predates these EDA file formats becoming common. Modern Arm CoreSight DAP IP delivery (DesignStart / DesignWare / Standard Cell Library partner deliverables) includes SDC + UPF + scan-insertion + boundary-scan-cell library files at the IP-license level. Custom SW-DP implementations (e.g. RISC-V Debug Module emulating ADIv5) supply their own constraints. SDC false-path on SWCLK→system-clock crossings and on SWDIO bidirectional control is the most common per-implementation constraint.
